exceptions.reason: The gas FAMILY is within tolerance (C2 PASS, +1.2%); the per-class C1 gate flags CC_REGULAR because the small family-level surplus concentrates in the marginal combined-cycle unit AND the per-class actual is deflated by the geothermal+biomass that NEISO folds into the EIA-930 'Natural Gas' cell (reconcile_vintage_classes subtracts ~1.6 TWh of NG-cell-folded non-gas from the gas target). The model books that OTHER/biomass residual (process gas / landfill / purchased steam) as its own measured must-run rows and serves the un-foldable remainder with marginal CC, so ~1 TWh of the gas the grid attributes to NG-cell-folded non-gas sources lands on CC_REGULAR. This is the same EIA-923-vs-EIA-930 OTHER categorization difference neiso-37/38 document, unchanged by the offer-curve consolidation (which changes no offer value). Closable only by reconciling the OTHER/NG-fold-in categorization on both sides, NEVER by injecting the residual or scaling CC to the deflated benchmark (fitting). Carried HARD caveat.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (structural; same winter fuel-inventory / reliability-commitment family as the C3c price-tail and C5b storage items)
exceptions.reason: Carried UNCHANGED from neiso-38 (the offer-curve consolidation changes no value, so coal/steam volumes are identical). The neiso-38 availability fix removed a definite overlay bug that had erased the energy (control coal 0.006/0.000/0.043 -> 0.058/0.113/0.234), but a residual under-run remains, largest in the LOW-gas years 2023/2024. Mechanism: the energy-only LP runs Merrimack and the lone steam unit only at the temperature-floor commitment plus the few hours delivered gas is dear enough to put coal (HR 11.337 x coal fuel ~ $30-45/MWh) genuinely in merit; in 2023/24 Henry Hub was $2.5/$2.2 and gas-CC out-competed coal most of the winter, so the LP holds coal near the floor. The REAL units ran more -- a winter fuel-security / local-reliability commitment (oil/coal/steam held online against multi-day cold-snap gas-deliverability risk) that a cost-based merit order cannot see, the SAME unobserved winter-scarcity driver behind the C3c >$300 tail and the C5b storage spread. The candidate forward-faithful lever (neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate) was tested in the neiso-38 session and does NOT close it (byte-identical: NEISO is not reserve-short, the dual-fuel oil fleet keeps the cold-window price at oil parity, so removing a small gas slice neither lifts price nor pulls more coal). Closable only by the documented future build that makes the winter oil/coal reliability commitment forward-reproducible (a fuel-inventory / seasonal-reliability constraint whose shadow price lands on the tightest cold hours and is condition-responsive), NEVER by cranking the floor slope/cap (regressed from measured CF) or by an offer adder. The 108 MW model bin for Merrimack (vs the real ~460 MW plant) bounds the maximum recoverable coal and is a separate fleet-representation item noted for follow-up.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent / reserve scarcity, capped here by the dual-fuel oil-parity)
exceptions.reason: Carried UNCHANGED from neiso-38. The model pins every top-price hour at the flat dual-fuel oil-parity cap (~$258/MWh): when delivered gas spikes on a cold day, dual-fuel units switch to oil (apply_dual_fuel_pricing) and the marginal price cannot exceed oil parity, so the energy-only LP produces 0 hours > $300. Two faithful ISO-NE scarcity structures (in-LP operating-reserve co-optimization on the published NEISO RCPF requirements; the temperature-dependent winter gas-availability derate inject_neiso_gas_coldsnap_derate) were re-confirmed NOT to bind in 2023-25: NEISO is not operating-reserve-short -- the ~6.8 GW dual-fuel fleet stays available on oil and imports/hydro/storage/floored-steam keep reserve headroom above the 1,800/1,200 MW requirements even with a 20% cold-window gas derate (reserve_price stays 0). Both are kept as default-off infrastructure that binds in tighter forecast years. The real residual driver is winter fuel-INVENTORY scarcity rent (oil/peaker units rationing limited on-site distillate over a multi-day cold snap); distillate is a global liquid fuel whose commodity price does not spike like pipeline gas basis, so a cold-day oil adder would be a forbidden residual fit. The only forward-faithful fix is modeling the oil fleet as inventory-limited (a seasonal oil-burn budget like hydro, whose shadow price IS the scarcity rent) -- a documented future build, not closable by an adder/offer tune. The offer-curve consolidation does not touch this (the 13.15x CT_PEAKER peak is unchanged; capping it in Step 2 would not create a >$300 hour because the dual-fuel oil parity caps the marginal price below the CT peak band in these years). Accepted caveat.

exceptions.classification: MODEL MISS (downstream of the price_tail / reserve-scarcity item)
exceptions.reason: Carried unchanged from neiso-38. Storage arbitrage throughput tracks the peak-to-trough price spread, which is compressed because the LP caps the cold-hour tail at the dual-fuel oil-parity (~$258, 0 hours > $300; see the price_tail caveat). The reserve co-optimization and gas-availability derate do not widen the spread in the backcast (NEISO is not reserve-short, reserve_price=0), and neither the Merrimack availability fix nor the offer-curve consolidation touches the price spread, so this is NOT a storage-model error: it closes only when the winter fuel-inventory scarcity rent is recovered via the forward-faithful oil-burn-budget constraint, never via a storage or offer tune.
